content.content: Show your work. Type the answer in the box. On the questions marked Steps, also type your steps (formula, numbers, answer, unit). Before you calculate, find the KEY WORD: inside = AREA (unit m²), around = PERIMETER (unit m).

AREA (m²): tile, carpet, paint, cover, floor, grass.   PERIMETER (m): fence, border, trim, frame, edge, ribbon or rope around.
Rectangle: area = l × w; perimeter = 2 × (l + w). Triangle: area = ½ × base × height. Circle: area = 3.14 × r × r (m²); circumference = 2 × 3.14 × r (m). Diameter = 2 × radius.

content.content: Two body systems work as a team. The respiratory system moves air: air goes down the windpipe into the lungs, where tiny air sacs called alveoli let oxygen pass into the blood. The circulatory system moves blood: red blood cells carry the oxygen, and the heart pumps the oxygen-rich blood to every cell. Cells use the oxygen and release carbon dioxide, a waste gas. The blood carries the carbon dioxide back to the lungs, and you breathe it out. Both systems speed up during exercise because working muscles need more oxygen and make more carbon dioxide.

pomodoros.subject: Social Studies: Courts and the 14th Amendment

content.content: The 14th Amendment (1868) says that no state may deny any person “the equal protection of the laws.” For decades, courts still allowed segregation. In Plessy v. Ferguson (1896), the Supreme Court upheld a “separate but equal” rule for railroad cars, and many states used the same idea to separate their schools. In Brown v. Board of Education (1954), the Court ruled that separate public schools for Black and white children were unequal by nature and therefore unconstitutional. Thurgood Marshall of the NAACP argued the case for the families. The decision shows judicial review at work: the judicial branch can strike down laws that conflict with the Constitution.

Timeline. 1868: 14th Amendment ratified.  1896: Plessy v. Ferguson.  1954: Brown v. Board of Education.  1956: Browder v. Gayle (a court rules against segregated buses; Claudette Colvin was one of the plaintiffs).
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.

content.content: Gladys West (born 1930) grew up on a farm in Virginia. “I realized I had to get an education to get out,” she told a newspaper in 2018. She finished first in her high school class, won a scholarship, and earned a mathematics degree at Virginia State College in 1952. In 1956 she began work as a mathematician at the Navy base at Dahlgren, Virginia, where she was one of only four Black employees. During a 42-year career there she used satellite data and early room-sized computers to help calculate the exact shape of the Earth. Her measurements contributed to the accuracy of GPS, the system that helps phones and cars find their way. (Practice passage written for this packet from published sources: IEEE Spectrum, 2024; Military Times, 2018.)
